question.text: What is the purpose of international cooperation provisions under PMLA?

answer.text: To enable the Central Government to enter into agreements with foreign governments for enforcing PMLA provisions, exchanging information, and investigating money laundering cases
To allow Indian citizens to open bank accounts in any foreign country without KYC requirements
To permit foreign banks to operate in India without complying with Indian AML regulations
To establish a common global currency to simplify tracking of cross-border financial transactions

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 56 of PMLA allows the Central Government to enter agreements with foreign governments for enforcing PMLA provisions and exchanging information for the prevention and investigation of offences, including assistance in matters connected to money laundering. The Trap: Options B, C, and D are distractors. Relaxing KYC for cross-border accounts, allowing foreign banks to bypass Indian AML rules, or creating a global currency are not the purpose of Section 56 — its purpose is to strengthen cross-border enforcement, not to weaken it. Note: International cooperation in AML also connects to the FATF Recommendations chapter (Recommendations 36-40) covered in NISM IFSCA-01.
